'''Chen Chuangtian''' ({{zh|s=陈创天}}; 18 February 1937 – 31 October 2018), also known as '''Chuang-Tian Chen''', was a Chinese [[materials scientist]] and [[physical chemist]] who specialized in crystals used in lasers. He discovered the [[Nonlinear optics|nonlinear optical]] crystals [[Beta barium borate|BBO]], [[Lithium triborate|LBO]] and KBBF, which have important uses in areas including [[superconductor]] research, semiconductor [[photolithography]], and the medical industry. He was an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] and a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]]. He was awarded the [[TWAS Prize]] in [[Chemistry]], the [[State Technological Invention Award]] (First Class), and the Laudise Prize.

== Biography ==
Chen was born on 18 February 1937 in [[Fenghua District|Fenghua]], [[Zhejiang]], China. He studied at Shenyang No. 2 High School, and was accepted by the Department of Physics of [[Peking University]] in August 1956.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/science/2018-02/18/c_136967179.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181104050258/http://www.xinhuanet.com/science/2018-02/18/c_136967179.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 4, 2018 |script-title=zh:1937年2月18日 材料科学专家陈创天诞生|date=2018-02-18|website=Xinhua|access-date=2018-11-01}}</ref> After graduating in 1962, he entered the Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter in [[Fuzhou]] on the recommendation of [[Hu Ning]], and studied under physical chemist [[Lu Jiaxi (chemist)|Lu Jiaxi]] for three years.<ref name=":1" />

In 1965, Chen chose [[Nonlinear optics|nonlinear optical]] materials as his research direction and spent the next two years calculating the nonlinear optical coefficients of many crystals.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://laser.ofweek.com/2018-11/ART-240001-8500-30278364.html |script-title=zh:纪念陈创天院士：让中国牌晶体誉享全球 KBBF晶体领先美国15年|date=2018-11-01|website=OFweek|access-date=2018-11-01}}</ref> In the late 1970s and the 1980s, Chen and his team discovered the new nonlinear optical crystals [[Beta barium borate|BaB<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> (BBO)]] and [[Lithium triborate|LiB<sub>3</sub>O<sub>5</sub> (LBO)]].<ref name=":1" />

In 1988, Chen and his team began searching for optical compounds that could produce shorter ultraviolet wavelengths. After researching hundreds of compounds, they discovered potassium beryllium fluoroborate (KBBF), a nonlinear optical crystal  which is capable of generating light within a very narrow bandwidth, with wavelengths of less than 200 nanometers.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/articles/oer/print/volume-16/issue-5/features/nonlinear-crystal-only-lsquomade-in-chinarsquo.html|title=Nonlinear crystal only 'made in China'|last=Wallace|first=John|date=2009-03-01|website=Laser Focus World|access-date=2018-11-02}}</ref> The crystal is important in [[superconductor]] research and can allow the replacement of [[excimer laser]] with [[Solid-state laser|solid-state]] ones in [[photolithography]] used in the semiconductor and the medical industries.<ref name=":2" /> Until at least 2009, Chen's laboratory at the Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter was the only place in the world that could produce KBBF.<ref name=":2" /> In 2013, Chen and his colleague {{ill|Xu Zuyan|zh|许祖彦}} invented the DUV-DPL device ([[deep ultraviolet]] [[diode-pumped solid-state laser]]), with a wavelength of only 177.3 nm.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.china.org.cn/china/2013-09/10/content_29984102.htm|title=China launches applicable deep UV laser device|last=Chen|first=Boyuan|date=2013-09-10|website=China.org.cn|access-date=2018-11-02}}</ref>

Chen died on 31 October 2018 in Beijing, at the age of 81.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://news.sciencenet.cn/htmlnews/2018/10/419368.shtm |script-title=zh:著名材料学家陈创天院士逝世|website=Sciencenet|access-date=2018-11-01}}</ref>

==Honors and recognition==
Chen was elected a fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] in 1990 and an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 2003.<ref name=":0" />

Chen was awarded the 1987 [[TWAS Prize]] in Chemistry, "for his outstanding contribution to the development of new nonlinear optical materials, the formulation of a quantum chemical theory that guides the search for such materials and the discovery of [[beta barium borate]] and [[lithium triborate]]".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twas.org/recipients-twas-awards-and-prizes|title=Recipients of TWAS Awards and Prizes|website=TWAS|language=en|access-date=2018-11-01}}</ref> He won a Special Prize of the Science and Technology Progress Award of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in 1986 for his discovery of BBO and the [[State Technological Invention Award]] (First Class) in 1991 for LBO.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.ipc.cas.cn/pe/cm/200708/t20070815_1346.html|title=Professor CHEN Chuangtian|website=Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry|access-date=2018-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805020318/http://english.ipc.cas.cn/pe/cm/200708/t20070815_1346.html|archive-date=2018-08-05|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2013, he was awarded the Laudise Prize by the International Organization for Crystal Growth.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iocg.org/prizes/index.html|title=Prizes|website=International Organization for Crystal Growth|language=en|access-date=2018-11-01|archive-date=2018-11-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181125185312/http://www.iocg.org/prizes/index.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://english.ipc.cas.cn/ns/es/201308/t20130822_108674.html|title=CAS Academician CHEN Chuangtian Receives Laudise Prize|date=2013-08-20|website=Technical Institute of Physics and Chemistry|access-date=2018-11-01}}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
